candidates.original_title: Age of acquisition effects depend on the mapping between representations and the frequency of occurrence: Empirical and computational evidence
candidates.description: Age of acquisition effects in picture and word naming as tested by Lambon Ralph and Ehsan (2006)
candidates.citation_sentence: In order to partially replicate the study of Lambon Ralph and Ehsan (2006), we followed their design and split our stimuli into early and late AoA and high-frequency and low-frequency words.

candidates.original_title: Age of acquisition effects depend on the mapping between representations and the frequency of occurrence: Empirical and computational evidence
candidates.description: Age of acquisition affects written word naming, with the magnitude of the effect differing from picture naming because orthography-to-phonology mappings are more systematic.
candidates.citation_sentence: In order to partially replicate the study of Lambon Ralph and Ehsan (2006), we followed their design and split our stimuli into early and late AoA and high-frequency and low-frequency words.
candidates.notes: Experiment 4 tested word-picture verification, written word naming, and corrected written word-naming latencies using word stimuli. The experiment showed mixed evidence across the component measures, including an opposite-direction effect in corrected latencies.

candidates.original_title: Age of acquisition effects depend on the mapping between representations and the frequency of occurrence: Empirical and computational evidence
candidates.description: Age of acquisition affects spoken picture naming, with the effect reflecting the arbitrary mapping between pictorial, semantic, and phonological representations.
candidates.citation_sentence: In order to partially replicate the study of Lambon Ralph and Ehsan (2006), we followed their design and split our stimuli into early and late AoA and high-frequency and low-frequency words.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 tested word-picture verification, spoken picture naming, and corrected spoken picture-naming latencies using pictorial stimuli. The experiment reproduced the expected age-of-acquisition pattern in picture naming, but included additional verification and subtraction measures beyond the original study.
